note: JUDGE-ONLY. Solvers must never read this.

corpus.repo: react/react (formerly facebook/react; moved to the React Foundation org — both URLs resolve)
corpus.verify: git -C $CORPUS rev-parse HEAD must equal the pinned commit before ANY run; if it moved, re-seed every oracle below on the new SHA before judging.
corpus.clone: git clone https://github.com/react/react.git packages/octocode-benchmark/context/react && git -C packages/octocode-benchmark/context/react checkout 9ceb1e7d9e20bd0302cf6ab31b038c5ec673178d
corpus.properties: Flow-typed .js (~1,873 files under packages/). tree-sitter-javascript cannot parse Flow annotations; both engines run error-recovery inside those files — a FEATURE of the corpus (real-world dirty input); the seeded oracles below already reflect it.

verificationCaveat: All numbers seeded 2026-08-02 on the pinned commit with ast-grep 0.45.0 and the local octocode build (post P1-prescan, post $$-guard). Parity questions still self-verify (both arms, same scope, same count) — but on a PINNED corpus the seeded values below are stable oracles; a mismatch means the SHA moved, the scope differed, or a tool regressed. The judge recomputes at run time on the pinned SHA.

harnessRules.note: Gotchas that produce false divergences — HARNESS errors, not tool findings. Apply before comparing counts.
rules: Line-number convention: ast-grep --json range.start.line is 0-BASED; octocode match lines are 1-BASED. Normalize (+1 on ast-grep) before diffing file:line sets.

File-set scope MUST be pinned: ast-grep '-l js' scans only .js; octocode structural with no include scans every supported extension (.ts test files too). Use include:["*.js"] on octocode — observed +8 phantom divergence in packages/react/src from one .ts test file.
Counting runs MUST lift octocode caps: maxFiles/itemsPerPage/maxMatchesPerFile well above the expected result size; verify stats.capReached is absent.
Metavar syntax: $X = one node, $$$X = list. octocode REJECTS $$X with a remediation message (2026-08-02+); ast-grep treats it as a never-matching literal.

octocode relative paths resolve against process cwd — always pass ABSOLUTE paths ($CORPUS/...). (A nonexistent path now errors loudly on every prefilter branch — fixed 2026-08-02; before that, literal-anchored patterns returned a silent 0.)

Flow ERROR-subtree divergence: inside Flow-annotated regions the engines recover differently — corpus-wide count divergence up to ~0.2% is expected and must be ATTRIBUTED (q3/q5), never scored as one tool 'wrong'.

Modifier semantics differ by design: octocode's bare `function $NAME(...)` does NOT match `async function` (explicit-modifier matching); ast-grep's does. Both match `export function` via the inner declaration node. Reconcile with explicit modifier patterns or a modifier-agnostic `kind: function_declaration` rule.
ast-grep 0.45 DOES ship yaml/json/markdown grammars AND an `outline` subcommand — never claim it lacks them; verify any grammar-gap claim at run time.
Time both arms per query (cold process) and record wall-clock as a guardrail; rerun any slow batch query solo before concluding failure.

q1.scoring: 1.0 exact count; 0.5 correct method with a capped count reported AS capped; 0 silent undercount.
q1.capabilityPoint: Structural call-shape parity: both arms must run a real AST pattern (useState($$$ARGS)), counts must match exactly; caps lifted.

q2.seededParity: ast-grep 50 == octocode 50 with IDENTICAL 1-based file:line sets (after +1 on ast-grep)
q2.scoring: 1.0 count + set match after normalization; 0.5 count only; 0 unexplained set mismatch.
q2.capabilityPoint: Exact-set parity: identical 1-based file:line sets after normalization -- catches off-by-one and truncation bugs, not just counts.

q3.expectedAttribution: All 10 ast-grep-only anchors sit on lines containing Flow generic syntax and NO .push call at all — ReactChildFiber.js:282 (function unwrapThenable<T>(thenable: Thenable<T>)), ReactFiberScope.js:36 (scopedNodes: Array<any>), ReactTestSelectors.js:232/272(x3)/430/587, ReactFiberPerformanceTrack.js:1238/1450. Mechanism: tree-sitter-javascript ERROR-subtree recovery on Flow annotations differs between engines.
q3.scoring: 1.0 both counts + mechanism + >=2 concrete file:line examples; 0.5 both counts + a 'Flow parse errors' hand-wave; 0 picking one count as 'the' answer or averaging.
q3.capabilityPoint: Divergence reconciliation: when tools disagree (342 vs 332), the arm must attribute every delta line to a concrete parser behavior (Flow generics), not hand-wave.

q4.oracle: await $X inside try_statement (stopBy: end) in $CORPUS/packages/react-devtools-shared/src, *.js scope
q4.seededParity: ast-grep 1 == octocode 1, same file. NOTE: octocode accepts the ast-grep rule YAML verbatim (pattern/inside/kind/stopBy).
q4.scoring: 1.0 count + file via a genuine relational rule; 0.5 count via a non-relational approximation; 0 wrong count.
q4.capabilityPoint: Relational rule parity: ast-grep YAML rule (inside try_statement, stopBy end) accepted verbatim by octocode structural mode.

seededWallClock.octocode: 1.74 s (node startup + count assembly; P2 push-down pending)

q5.scoring: 1.0 count matching the seeded pair for the tool(s) run + honest wall-clock + divergence attributed if both were run; 0.5 one tool with caps provably lifted; 0 a capped count presented as the total.
q5.guardrail: A solver reporting both tools agreeing EXACTLY on this corpus is suspect — recompute before accepting.
q5.capabilityPoint: Scale census: whole-corpus (~1,873 files) structural count under lifted caps; divergence must be reported with percentage, wall-clock recorded.

q6.astGrepCeiling: Pattern search finds name SHAPES but cannot prove identity (imports, aliasing, shadowing, strings/comments). Full credit requires a symbol-resolving method (LSP references or equivalent) or per-hit identity verification.
q6.scoring: 1.0 5 files + counts + identity-safe method; 0.5 right files, counts polluted by comments/strings; 0 a grep dump presented as callers.

q7.oracle: localFindDeadCode on $CORPUS/packages/scheduler: 28 files scanned; candidates include feature-flag consts (enableProfiling — once per SchedulerFeatureFlags fork — frameYieldMs, userBlockingPriorityTimeout, normalPriorityTimeout, lowPriorityTimeout, enableRequestPaint, enableAlwaysYieldScheduler, runIdCounter, compare); the tool itself reports confidence 'low'.
q7.astGrepCeiling: Cannot express reachability — an export-without-import text join is acceptable ONLY with the verification step.
q7.judgeNote: scheduler has forked SchedulerFeatureFlags variants rooted externally by www/native builds — being flagged does NOT prove deletable. The question grades verification discipline, not deletion.
q7.scoring: 1.0 candidate list + 2 independent verifications + honest confidence; 0.5 list without verification; 0 'no dead code' or unverified delete claims.

expected.ratioCeiling: outline must be <= 11% of full-file bytes to count as a condensed surface
expected.note: BOTH toolchains have an outline surface (ast-grep 0.45 `outline`; octocode minify:'symbols' / documentSymbols — 99 top-level functions via native-graph-facts). Byte counts include different content (bare lines vs JSON envelope with signatures); judge on ratio + symbol-count correctness, not raw bytes alone.

q8.scoring: 1.0 ~99 symbols + bytes + ratio; 0.5 outline produced, symbol count wrong/unreported; 0 full-file read presented as an outline.
q8.capabilityPoint: Condensed-surface parity: both arms produce an outline <= 11% of full-file bytes; compares outline byte cost head-to-head.

q9.oracle: scheduleUpdateOnFiber body spans lines 973-1099 (127 lines, ~5.5 KB source) of ReactFiberWorkLoop.js
q9.expected: returned bytes for the slice < 8 KB; a full-file read (203 KB) scores 0
q9.scoring: 1.0 correct window + < 8 KB; 0.5 right window padded past 8 KB; 0 whole-file read.
q9.capabilityPoint: Bounded read: ghGetFileContent/localGetFileContent matchString slice (or startLine/endLine window) returns only the function body; ast-grep has no bounded-reader surface -- the arm must show how it avoided the 203 KB full-file read.

q10.oracle: flushSyncWork is defined at $CORPUS/packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberWorkLoop.js:1934 (export function flushSyncWork(): boolean). Distractors: flushSyncWorkOnAllRoots / flushSyncWorkOnLegacyRootsOnly at ReactFiberRootScheduler.js:171/177 — an exact-symbol method must NOT return those.
q10.expected: file:line 1934; <= 4 tool calls excellent, <= 6 acceptable; byte accounting across all steps required
q10.scoring: 1.0 exact file:line + distractors excluded + call/byte accounting; 0.5 found with extra manual steps; 0 wrong symbol (prefix match) or no accounting.
q10.capabilityPoint: Composite flow: exact-symbol resolution (lspGetSemantics definition or structural exact match) that rejects the flushSyncWorkOnAllRoots/OnLegacyRootsOnly distractors, chained with a bounded read -- text search alone cannot disambiguate; grade call count + byte accounting.
